subject: MAP: Nimbus performance evaluation & hosting behavior comparison
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff + proposed benchmarking plan (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — excited to get the MAP and the evaluation plan running. Attached is a first-pass MAP and the benchmarking toolkit I mentioned (nimbus_MAP_v1.pdf, benchmarking_script.tar.gz). High-level ask from our side: 3-week evaluation window where we run a controlled set of benchmarks across your three hosting options (Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private) and deliver a short results pack that maps to your SLA & procurement questions.

Proposed cadence:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP and test accounts; procurement loop (procurement@nimbushealth.com) included.
- Week 1: dry-run + Hosted baseline (cold start and warm cache).
- Week 2: Dedicated pool test (steady-state throughput + autoscale stress).
- Week 3: Private deployment (network isolation + predictability checks) + wrap.

Measurement plan (we'll record p50/p90/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), TTFT (time-to-first-token), and concurrency scaling across 1/8/32/64 virtual clients). Isolation checks: run noisy-neighbor injection during Dedicated tests to validate SLA fallbacks. Autoscaling behavior: measure queue build-up and time to target throughput when load steps up 4x.

Next steps: please confirm the evaluation window and any compliance artifacts you need up front. If that looks fine I will share a short onboarding checklist and a Drive folder with scripts and sample workloads.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Connor — thanks for the plan and the quick turnaround. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates: 
1) For the Private deployment we will need an on-site ops window (our infra team needs to approve network configs). Can we schedule that for Week 3?
2) What footprint (GPU spec / vCPU / memory) do you recommend for the Dedicated pool to match production-like throughput?
3) Can you confirm data egress and logging behavior — procurement asked about audit logs and retention defaults.

We're targeting an internal decision by May 26; procurement is on the thread for any commercial docs.

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 May 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + proposed benchmarking plan (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Alice — answers inline and a slightly more prescriptive test matrix attached.

1) Private deployment ops window: yes — Week 3 works. We'll provide a network checklist (ports, peering, KMS endpoints) and a 2-hour on-call window for your infra team.

2) Dedicated footprint recommendation: start with 2 x A100 40GB equiv (or 4 x A10G equiv) for the initial Dedicated pool to reproduce expected concurrency patterns. We'll include a scaled-down run at 1/2 capacity to verify linear scaling assumptions.

3) Audit logs & data egress: Hosted API uses our standard retention policy (30 days request logs, 365 days billing metadata) — we'll provide SOC2 evidence in the MAP attachments. Dedicated has customer-isolated logs with customer-managed retention; Private deployment pushes logs to your KMS/collector per config. I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a short table mapping retention by deployment in the Drive link.

Attached is a compact test matrix (also pasted below):

Test matrix (examples)
- Baseline (Hosted): 3 workloads — short chat (avg 40 tokens), summarization (avg 600 tokens), embeddings batch (1500 items)
  - Concurrency: 1, 8, 32; capture p50/p90/p95, tokens/sec, TTFT (cold/warm).
- Dedicated: same workloads; add noisy-neighbor job (synthetic 60% GPU load) to test isolation and fallback routing.
- Private: same workloads; focus on network jitter + cold-start times and predictability over 6h steady-state.

Metrics of interest for your procurement + infra:
- Predictability: stddev(p95) across windows, pct of requests > SLA bound.
- Autoscale behavior: ramp-up time to target throughput after 4x step and peak queue lengths.
- Cost proxies: tokens/sec per GPU-hour, median TTL of KV cache hits.

We'll run the Hosted baseline first and share raw CSVs (results-hosted-dedicated-private.csv). Rishi will run the initial Hosted pass tomorrow morning and feed results into the Drive folder.

Connor

Attachments: updated_test_matrix.md, SOC2-summary.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 May 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + proposed benchmarking plan (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) — initial Hosted pass

Quick update from the Hosted baseline run (attached CSV has full trace):
- Workload: short chat (avg 40 tokens), concurrency sweep [1,8,32] on p3-like instance class
- Observed (median across 5 runs):
  • p50 latency: 48 ms
  • p90 latency: 132 ms
  • p95 latency: 225 ms
  • TTFT (cold): 420 ms; TTFT (warm): 38 ms
  • tokens/sec (aggregate @32 clients): 18,400 tokens/sec
- Notes: variability increases at higher concurrency due to KV cache eviction patterns; we saw one autoscale event at a synthetic load spike that added ~220ms extra p95 for ~3 minutes during scale-up.

Next for Dedicated: we'll spin a 2xA100-equivalent pool and run the same sweep with and without noisy-neighbor at 60% background load. Expect to have Dedicated traces by Friday.

Rishi
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@nimbushealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP interim summary + ask (decision checkpoint)

Alice — attaching the interim results pack and a short recommendation to help with your internal decision (Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNIMBUS_MAP_DEMO). Key takeaways: 
- Hosted gives the lowest friction and good median latency; p95 variability under synthetic scale-up is the primary caveat.
- Dedicated delivers more predictable p95 under steady-state and is resilient to modest noisy-neighbor injection when sized per our recommended footprint.
- Private adds the strongest isolation guarantees but requires the on-site ops window and additional network validation time (adds ~3 business days to cutover).

Requested next step from Nimbus: confirm which path you want to pilot (Hosted quick-win vs Dedicated reserved trial vs Private POC). Procurement, please advise if you need a commercial addendum for Dedicated capacity. If you approve Dedicated trial, we'll prepare a short SOW and a DocuSign envelope for signature: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?po=1a2b3c4d5e

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call to walk through the CSVs.

Marissa Cole
Manager, Enterprise Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
